research_question: Does recent non-routine insider purchase support identify Rush episodes with lower subsequent large-pullback or structural-break risk?

economic_hypothesis.interpretation_if_passed: Protective veto evidence against premature profit-taking; never a buy or sell trigger by itself.
economic_hypothesis.forbidden_inverse: Absence of purchase support must not be interpreted as evidence to sell.

population.universe: Eligible current S&P 500 constituents excluding the existing 51 equities.
population.claim_boundary: Hypothesis-specific current-constituent OOS robustness; not blind and not survivorship safe.

feature_definition.availability_rule: filingDate must be strictly earlier than signal_date
feature_definition.routine_rule: At the filing date, the same owner and issuer had qualifying P purchases in the same calendar month in each of the three immediately preceding calendar years.
feature_definition.warmup_rule: Before three full prior calendar years are observable for that owner-issuer pair, routine status is UNKNOWN and the event cannot create the feature.
feature_definition.non_routine_rule: After warmup, a qualifying event not matching the routine rule is a non-routine purchase-support candidate.
feature_definition.aggregation: Episode feature is 1 when at least one qualifying non-routine owner event is publicly available in the lookback window.

evidence_basis.claim: Insider purchases have historically been more informative than sales.
Purchase portfolios earned abnormal returns while sale portfolios did not in the cited historical sample.
Routine insider trades were substantially less informative than opportunistic trades.
